17/2/2019



Dr G Stark

Surgeon

Department of Thoracic Medicine

Smithtown Hospital

Smithtown



Dear Dr Stark,

Re: James Smith, DOB: 26/10/2004



I am writing to request a possible bilateral lung transplant for James, who is being discharged from our
                                                                                                            19/8/20 11:07 AM
hospital today.
                                                                                                            Comment [1]: This is a singular countable
                                                                                                            noun mentioned for the first time, so the
                                                                                                            indefinite article ‘a’ is used.

Regarding James’s medical history, he has cystic fibrosis, chronic sinus infections and symptomatic focal
epilepsy. In term of medications, he takes paracetamol, Pulmozyme, phenytoin and Creon. Please note,
he has sedentary lifestyle.
                                                                                                            19/8/20 11:07 AM
                                                                                                            Comment [2]: This information is not as
                                                                                                            relevant to the chief complaint so it can come
                                                                                                            later in the letter.
On 02/02/2019, James presented complaining of lower respiratory tract infection symptoms. Although
his breathing rate was high, his oxygen saturation was low. On examination, he had an erythematous
oropharynx, sonorous wheeze and bibasal crackles. As a result, ampicillin sulbactam was prescribed.
One day later, his chest x-ray revealed pleural effusion and pneumonia, and his CT scan result showed
chronic paranasal sinusitis. Therefore, azithromycin and ciprofloxacin were added.
                                                                                                            19/8/20 11:12 AM
                                                                                                            Comment [3]: Great summary!


Today, James was recovering well. However, he has a tendency for frequent lung infections for which an
increase in hospital visits and home schooling was recommended. His discharge plan includes referral to
a physiotherapist for airway clearance technique and to a dietitian to improve his lifestyle.
 
In light of the information above, your surgical intervention of James’s condition would be greatly
appreciated. If you require any further clarification, please do not hesitate to get contact me.
                                                                                                      19/8/20 11:10 AM
                                                                                                      Comment [4]: Just use ‘contact’ as the
                                                                                                      verb. …do not hesitate to contact me.
Yours sincerely,

Doctor

                   the medical history. Despite this, the content choice is appropriate,
